claim: 68% of South Asian adults are vitamin D deficient (serum 25(OH)D <20 ng/mL), based on pooled meta-analysis of 65 studies across 5 countries.
stance_target: Vitamin D deficiency is highly prevalent in South Asia including India, justifying supplementation products
scope_conditions: Adults 18+ years in Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, Nepal, Sri Lanka; studies published 2001-2019
quoted_support: This study reveals that 68% [95% CI: 64 to 72%] of the SA adults are affected with vitamin D deficiency.

claim: India's pooled vitamin D deficiency prevalence is approximately 68% based on 39 studies covering 38,672 participants, with a weighted mean vitamin D level of 16.14 ng/mL.
stance_target: Indian population has very high rates of vitamin D deficiency warranting supplementation
scope_conditions: Indian adults; 39 studies included; majority cross-sectional hospital or community-based
quoted_support: We found 39 studies from India which consisted of 38,672 participants... The weighted mean level of vitamin D for study participants was 16.14296 ng/mL (weighted SD 4.83 ng/mL)

claim: Vitamin D deficiency prevalence in individual Indian studies ranges from 17% to 99%, with the wide range reflecting urban/rural, demographic, and seasonal variation.
stance_target: Vitamin D deficiency is pervasive but heterogeneous across Indian population segments
scope_conditions: India-specific studies included in systematic review
quoted_support: Prevalence of vitamin D deficiency ranged from 17 to 99% and the average vitamin D level ranged from 4.7 to 32 ng/mL

claim: Female South Asian adults have a substantially higher vitamin D deficiency prevalence (76%) than males (51%), likely due to limited outdoor activity and clothing practices.
stance_target: Women are a higher-risk target demographic for vitamin D supplementation in South Asia
scope_conditions: South Asian adults; gender-stratified analysis; 25 female-only and 5 male-only studies
quoted_support: Gender-wise comparison in our study reveals that females could be affected with vitamin D deficiency more than the males in SA; 76% for females (95% CI: 68 to 82%) as opposed to 51% for males (95% CI: 41-61%)

claim: No national-level nutritional guidelines for vitamin D were found in any South Asian country at the time of the review, representing a significant policy gap.
stance_target: The Indian supplement market addresses a gap unmet by government nutritional policy
quoted_support: our search did not reveal any national level nutritional guidelines for vitamin D in any South Asian countries.

claim: Vitamin D deficiency in South Asia is described as a 'public health emergency' by the study authors, with approximately 1 billion people worldwide affected.
stance_target: Vitamin D supplementation addresses a major public health challenge
quoted_support: The high prevalence of vitamin D deficiency among SA adults is a public health challenge that should be addressed as an emergency, some even argue whether this should be treated as an ongoing pandemic.

claim: Pakistan had the highest country-level vitamin D deficiency prevalence in South Asia at 73%, while Sri Lanka had the lowest at 48%.
stance_target: Country-level variation in South Asian vitamin D deficiency
scope_conditions: South Asian adults; country-level forest plot analysis
quoted_support: Country-wise comparison showed that Sri Lanka had the lowest percentage (48%) of prevalence, while Pakistan had the highest (73%).

claim: Urban populations in India show higher vitamin D deficiency rates than rural populations, consistent with indoor lifestyle and pollution reducing UV-B exposure.
stance_target: Urbanization is a key risk factor for vitamin D deficiency in India
scope_conditions: India; of 39 studies: 17 urban, 3 rural, 6 mixed
quoted_support: Out of 39 studies, 17 studies were conducted among urban populations, 3 studies on the rural population and 6 studies were conducted on population from both rural and urban areas.
